content_units: Cold-Start Rough Idle: Most Likely Causes on a 2015 Corolla
Your pattern points most strongly to a   cold-start fuel/air/ignition issue   rather than a major mechanical failure, because:
- It happens mainly in the   first 2 minutes after startup
- The   check-engine light is intermittent
-   Fuel economy is slightly worse
- Once warm, the car   drives normally
On a 2015 Toyota Corolla, the most likely causes are usually:
-   Dirty or sticking mass airflow sensor (MAF)
-   Vacuum leak   that is worse when the engine is cold
-   Weak ignition coil or early misfire issue
-   Fuel injector with poor spray pattern/dribbling
-   Throttle body or intake carbon buildup
- Less commonly:   coolant temperature sensor reading wrong  ,   PCV-related air leak  , or   early head gasket/coolant seep issue
Diagnostic Checklist a Mechanic Would Usually Follow
Step   Action   What to Check   Expected Result
1   Scan stored codes   Misfire codes, fuel trim, MAF, coolant temp data   Points to cylinder/fuel-air direction
2   Cold-start live data test   Coolant temp vs ambient, short/long fuel trims   Sensor or mixture issue becomes visible
3   Inspect intake/vacuum system   Cracked hoses, loose clamps, PCV leaks   Air leak found if trims are lean
4   Check MAF and throttle body   Dirt/oil contamination, airflow reading at idle   Dirty readings often improve after cleaning
5   Misfire isolation   Coil swap test, plug inspection, injector balance   Misfire follows bad coil/injector
6   Fuel and coolant checks   Fuel pressure, injector leakage, coolant loss   Confirms delivery or internal leak issue
Most Likely Faults Ranked by Probability and Cost
1) Dirty MAF sensor or throttle body carbon
- Very common for   rough cold idle   and   slight MPG drop
- A dirty MAF can under-report airflow, causing a lean cold-start mixture
- Carbon around the throttle plate can upset idle airflow before warmup settles it
Typical diagnosis:
- Scan for fuel trims and airflow readings
- Inspect and clean MAF with proper MAF cleaner
- Inspect/clean throttle body
Typical repair cost:
-   Low-cost   if cleaning solves it
- More if the   MAF sensor itself needs replacement  , but still usually moderate
2) Small vacuum leak / PCV hose leak / intake gasket seep
- Cold engines are more sensitive to unmetered air
- A small leak often causes   rough idle cold  , then becomes less noticeable warm
- Can also trigger intermittent lean or misfire codes
Typical diagnosis:
- Fuel trim check during cold idle
- Smoke test of intake system
- Inspect PCV hose, intake duct, manifold area
Typical repair cost:
-   Low-cost   for a hose, clamp, or PCV issue
-   Moderate   if an intake gasket is involved
3) Weak ignition coil causing a cold misfire
- Coils can fail intermittently before fully dying
- A weak coil may misfire most when cold, then improve once heat changes resistance and combustion stabilizes
- Spark plugs were replaced 30,000 km ago, so plugs are less likely but still should be inspected
Typical diagnosis:
- Read misfire counters by cylinder
- Swap suspect coil to another cylinder and see if the misfire follows
- Inspect plug condition and oil contamination in plug wells
Typical repair cost:
-   Low-cost to moderate   if one coil is replaced
- Usually not a major repair
4) Fuel injector partially clogged or leaking down
- Can cause rough running immediately after startup
- A leaking injector can create a rich stumble; a restricted one can create a lean misfire
- Slight MPG drop fits this possibility
Typical diagnosis:
- Misfire data by cylinder
- Injector balance test or listening test
- Fuel pressure leak-down test
- Sometimes borescope or plug reading after cold soak
Typical repair cost:
-   Moderate
- Cleaning may be cheaper; replacement raises cost
5) Engine coolant temperature sensor reading inaccurately
- If the ECU thinks the engine is warmer than it is, cold-start enrichment may be too low
- Can cause rough idle only when cold, with normal operation once actually warm
Typical diagnosis:
- Compare coolant temp reading to true ambient after overnight sit
- Check sensor wiring and connector
Typical repair cost:
- Usually   low-cost to moderate
6) Early head gasket seep or coolant intrusion
- Less likely than the items above, but important if there is:
- unexplained coolant loss
- sweet exhaust smell on startup
- white vapor beyond normal cold condensation
- one-cylinder misfire mainly on first startup
Typical diagnosis:
- Check coolant level trend
- Inspect plugs for one steam-cleaned cylinder
- Combustion gas test / pressure test / borescope
Typical repair cost:
-   Expensive
- This is the main high-cost scenario on the list
Low-Cost vs Expensive Repairs
Usually low-cost
- MAF sensor cleaning
- Throttle body cleaning
- Vacuum hose or intake duct repair
- PCV valve or PCV hose service
- Coolant temperature sensor replacement
- Single ignition coil replacement
Usually moderate
- MAF sensor replacement
- Intake manifold gasket replacement
- Injector cleaning or one injector replacement
- Fuel system diagnosis and minor fuel delivery repairs
Usually expensive
- Multiple injector replacement
- Major fuel pressure system repairs
- Internal engine repair
- Head gasket repair
Best-Fit Diagnosis for Your Symptoms
Most likely order for your Corolla:
1.   Dirty MAF / throttle body
2.   Small vacuum leak or PCV-related leak
3.   Single-cylinder cold misfire from a weak coil
4.   Injector issue
5.   Coolant temp sensor
6.   Head gasket/coolant intrusion

The clue is that it is   cold-only, brief, and then normal once warm  . That usually means the mechanic will focus first on   fuel trims, misfire counters, intake leaks, MAF readings, and coil behavior during the first cold start  .
